title: Children of the Magenta (Automation Paradox, pt. 1)

sentences.en: On the evening of May 31st, 2009, 216 passengers, three pilots, and nine flight attendants boarded an Air France flight in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
sentences.zh: 2009年5月31日傍晚，216名乘客、3名飞行员和9名乘务员在巴西里约热内卢登上了一架法航航班。

sentences.en: The flight was headed across the Atlantic Ocean to Paris.
sentences.zh: 这架飞机正飞越大西洋前往巴黎。

sentences.en: A warning, this story might not be a good one to listen to if you're sitting on a plane right now.
sentences.zh: 温馨提示，如果你现在正坐在飞机上，这个故事可能不太适合听。

sentences.en: That's producer Katie Mingle letting you know that the closest exit could be behind you.
sentences.zh: 那是制作人凯蒂·明格（Katie Mingle）提醒你，最近的紧急出口可能在你的身后。

sentences.en: The plane that took off that evening from Rio was an Airbus 330.
sentences.zh: 当晚从里约起飞的飞机是一架空客A330。

sentences.en: The plane reached a cruising altitude of 35,000 feet.
sentences.zh: 飞机爬升到了35,000英尺的巡航高度。

sentences.en: The passengers read and watched movies and slept.
sentences.zh: 乘客们阅读、看电影、睡觉。

sentences.en: As they flew over the Atlantic Ocean, passing the equator,
sentences.zh: 当他们飞越大西洋、穿过赤道时，

sentences.en: There was a lot of thunderstorm activity.

sentences.zh: 这是伊沙（Isha）的威廉·朗（William Long）。

sentences.en: He wrote an article for Vanity Fair about this flight and has written extensively about aviation.
sentences.zh: 他曾为《名利场》杂志撰写过关于这次航班的文章，并对航空业进行过广泛报道。

sentences.en: He also used to be a pilot.
sentences.zh: 他以前还是一名飞行员。

sentences.en: So I spent many, many thousands of hours in cockpits.
sentences.zh: 所以我曾在驾驶舱里度过了许许多多的数千小时。

sentences.en: Which means he's particularly well-suited to tell the story of Air France flight 447.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他特别适合讲述法国航空447号航班的故事。

sentences.en: So they had two co-pilots, known as first officers, and one captain.
sentences.zh: 所以他们有两名副驾驶（被称为大副）和一名机长。

sentences.en: They would fly the plane in shifts, two of them flying while one slept.
sentences.zh: 他们会轮流驾驶飞机，其中两人驾驶，一人睡觉。

sentences.en: We know that the flight proceeded normally for several hours.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，飞行在头几个小时里进展正常。

sentences.en: Then, with no communication to the ground or air traffic control, it suddenly disappeared.
sentences.zh: 然后，在与地面或空中交通管制没有任何通信的情况下，它突然消失了。

sentences.en: Some pieces of the plane and several bodies were found days later floating in the Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 几天后，人们在大西洋上发现了飞机的一些碎片和几具漂浮的遗体。

sentences.en: But it would be two more years before most of the wreckage was found deep in the ocean.
sentences.zh: 但又过了两年，大部分残骸才在深海中被找到。

sentences.en: All 228 people on board had died.
When the wreckage was found, they also recovered the cockpit voice recorder and the flight data recorders.
sentences.zh: 当残骸被找到时，他们还打捞出了驾驶舱语音记录器和飞行数据记录器。

sentences.en: And they were in good shape.
The recordings were able to tell a story about how Flight 447 ended up in the bottom of the Atlantic Ocean.
sentences.zh: 这些录音记录揭示了447号航班最终如何坠入大西洋底的故事。

sentences.en: And the story they told was about what happened when the automated system flying the plane suddenly shut off.
sentences.zh: 他们讲述的故事是关于当驾驶飞机的自动化系统突然关闭时发生了什么。

sentences.en: And the pilots were left surprised, confused, and ultimately unable to fly their own plane.
sentences.zh: 而飞行员们感到惊讶、困惑，最终无力驾驶自己的飞机。

sentences.en: Automation in flight has been around for a long time.
sentences.zh: 飞行自动化已经存在很长时间了。

sentences.en: The first so-called autopilot was invented by the Sperry Corporation in 1912.
sentences.zh: 第一个所谓的自动驾驶仪是由斯佩里公司（Sperry Corporation）于1912年发明的。

sentences.en: And it allowed the plane to fly straight and level without the pilot's intervention.
sentences.zh: 它允许飞机在没有飞行员干预的情况下保持直线和平稳飞行。

sentences.en: In the 1950s, the autopilots got better.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪50年代，自动驾驶仪变得更好了。

sentences.en: So that you could program an autopilot to follow a route, not just to keep the wings level.
sentences.zh: 因此你可以编程让自动驾驶仪遵循一条航线，而不仅仅是保持机翼水平。

sentences.en: This was making the pilot's job a lot easier.
sentences.zh: 这大大减轻了飞行员的工作。

sentences.en: But there was still a lot to think about in the cockpit of an airplane.
sentences.zh: 但在飞机驾驶舱里仍然有很多需要考虑的事情。

sentences.en: Controlling the electric systems, controlling the hydraulic systeMs.
sentences.zh: 控制电气系统，控制液压系统。

sentences.en: And because of all this, most planes had three people in the cockpit.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，大多数飞机的驾驶舱里都有三个人。
两名飞行员和一个工程师。

sentences.en: Flight engineers sat behind the pilots, and they manipulated and managed these increasingly complex systeMs.
sentences.zh: 飞行工程师坐在飞行员身后，他们操作和管理这些日益复杂的系统。

sentences.en: But by the 1970s, all of those complex systems were also automated.
sentences.zh: 但到了20世纪70年代，所有这些复杂的系统也实现了自动化。

sentences.en: And flight engineers lost their necessity and their jobs.
sentences.zh: 飞行工程师失去了其必要性和工作。

sentences.en: By this time, the jet engine had replaced the piston engine, making planes much more reliable.
sentences.zh: 此时，喷气发动机已经取代了活塞发动机，使飞机变得更加可靠。

sentences.en: And studies were showing that most accidents were being caused not by mechanical error, but by human error.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，大多数事故不是由机械错误引起的，而是由人为错误引起的。

sentences.en: And a French company called Airbus thought that they could make planes safer by letting automation carry an even bigger part of the burden of flying.
sentences.zh: 一家名为空中客车（Airbus）的法国公司认为，他们可以通过让自动化承担更大比例的飞行负担来使飞机更安全。

sentences.en: Airbus has always been quite radical in its design philosophy.
sentences.zh: 空客在其设计理念上一直相当激进。

sentences.en: Led by a guy named Bernard Ziegler, Airbus set out to design what they hoped would be the safest plane yet.
sentences.zh: 在伯纳德·齐格勒（Bernard Ziegler）的领导下，空客着手设计他们希望是有史以来最安全的飞机。

sentences.en: A plane that even the worst pilots could fly with ease.
sentences.zh: 一架连最糟糕的飞行员也能轻松驾驶的飞机。

sentences.en: Bernard Ziegler, he famously said that he was building an airplane that his concierge could fly.
sentences.zh: 伯纳德·齐格勒曾有一句名言：他正在制造一架连他的礼宾员都能驾驶的飞机。

sentences.en: Ziegler's plane not only had autopilot, it also had what's called a fly-by-wire system.
sentences.zh: 齐格勒的飞机不仅有自动驾驶仪，还有所谓的电传操纵系统（fly-by-wire）。

sentences.en: So this can get a bit technical, but basically an autopilot just does what a pilot tells it to do.
sentences.zh: 这可能会变得有点技术性，但基本上自动驾驶仪只是做飞行员告诉它要做的事情。

sentences.en: Fly-by-wire is a computer-based control system that can interpret what the pilot wants to do and then do it smoothly and safely.
sentences.zh: 电传操纵系统是一个基于计算机的控制系统，可以解释飞行员想要做什么，然后平稳安全地执行。

sentences.en: So if the pilot pulls back on his or her stick, the fly-by-wire system will say,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果飞行员向后拉动他或她的操纵杆，电传操纵系统会说，

sentences.en: Oh, I see that you want to pitch up, and here, I'll do it for you at just the right angle and rate.
sentences.zh: 哦，我明白你想抬头，来吧，我以恰好的角度和速率为你完成。

sentences.en: Importantly, the fly-by-wire system will also protect you from getting into an aerodynamic stall.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，电传操纵系统还会保护你免于进入气动失速。

sentences.en: So in a car, a stall happens when the engine stops turning.
sentences.zh: 所以在汽车里，失速发生在发动机停止转动时。

sentences.en: But in a plane, stalling is different.
sentences.zh: 但在飞机中，失速是不同的。

sentences.en: Basically getting so slow that the wings no longer function correctly and the airplane, you know, loses altitude, put it that way.
sentences.zh: 基本上是速度变得如此之慢，以至于机翼不再正常工作，飞机，你知道的，失去了高度，这么说吧。

sentences.en: A stall in a plane can happen when the nose of the plane is pitched up at too steep an angle.
sentences.zh: 飞机失速可能发生在机头以过陡的角度仰起时。

sentences.en: A steep angle can cause the plane to lose lift and start to descend.
sentences.zh: 陡峭的角度会导致飞机失去升力并开始下降。

sentences.en: Stalling in a plane is not good.
sentences.zh: 飞机失速可不是什么好事。

sentences.en: Stall for long enough and you will crash.
sentences.zh: 失速时间足够长，你就会坠毁。

sentences.en: But fly-by-wire automation makes it impossible to do, as long as it's on.
sentences.zh: 但只要开启，电传操纵自动化就会使这种情况不可能发生。

sentences.en: Unlike autopilot, the fly-by-wire system cannot be turned on and off by the pilot.
sentences.zh: 与自动驾驶仪不同，电传操纵系统不能由飞行员手动开启和关闭。

sentences.en: You can't turn this automation off.
sentences.zh: 你无法关闭这种自动化。

sentences.en: And that's exactly what it did on May 31st, 2009, as flight 447 flew through the night sky over the Atlantic Ocean.
sentences.zh: 这正是2009年5月31日发生的事情，当时447号航班正飞越夜空中大西洋上空。

sentences.en: At some point, having flown normally for a few hours, the captain had gone back to sleep.
sentences.zh: 在正常飞行了几个小时后的某个时刻，机长回去睡觉了。

sentences.en: This meant the two co-pilots were in control of the plane.
sentences.zh: 这意味着两名副驾驶在控制飞机。
他们从未遇到过显著的湍流。

sentences.en: So far, nothing out of the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 突然，他们失去了空速指示。

sentences.en: A pressure probe on the outside of the plane had iced over.
sentences.zh: 飞机外侧的一个压力探头结冰了。

sentences.en: The automation could no longer tell how fast the plane was going.
sentences.zh: 自动化系统再也无法判断飞机的飞行速度了。

sentences.en: At the same time, the fly-by-wire system degraded by one step.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，电传操纵系统降级了一步。

sentences.en: So the autopilot turned off and the fly-by-wire system shifted into a different mode.
sentences.zh: 因此，自动驾驶仪关闭，电传操纵系统切换到了另一种模式。

sentences.en: A mode that did not protect against aerodynamic stall.
sentences.zh: 一种不提供防止气动失速保护的模式。

sentences.en: None of this was ideal, but it also wasn't a reason to panic, according to William.
sentences.zh: 根据威廉的说法，这一切都不是理想状态，但也还算不上恐慌的理由。

sentences.en: The plane was still basically flying straight and steady.
sentences.zh: 飞机基本上仍在笔直稳定地飞行。

sentences.en: Had they done nothing, they would have done exactly what they needed to do.
sentences.zh: 如果他们什么都不做，他们就已经做了完全需要做的事情。

sentences.en: The co-pilot in the right seat put his hand on his control stick.
sentences.zh: 右座的副驾驶把手放在了他的操纵杆上。

sentences.en: A little joystick-like thing to his right.
sentences.zh: 一个在他右侧的类似小操纵杆的东西。

sentences.en: He pulled it three-quarters of the way back.
sentences.zh: 他把它拉回了四分之三。

sentences.en: Why he did that is a major question.
sentences.zh: 他为什么要这么做是一个主要问题。

sentences.en: Perhaps he was startled or reacting to some turbulence.
sentences.zh: 也许他受到了惊吓，或者在对某种湍流做出反应。

sentences.en: It's important to note that he did not tell the other pilot in the cockpit,
sentences.zh: 重要的是要注意，他没有告诉驾驶舱里的另一名飞行员，

sentences.en: the guy in the left seat, what he had just done.
sentences.zh: 左座的那个人，他刚刚做了什么。

sentences.en: If he had, maybe his co-pilot would have known the dangerous situation they were about to be in.
sentences.zh: 如果他说了，也许他的副驾驶就会知道他们即将陷入危险境地。

sentences.en: In an Airbus, the two pilots have separate control sticks that move independently of each other.
sentences.zh: 在空客飞机上，两名飞行员拥有各自独立的操纵杆，彼此独立移动。

sentences.en: In other commercial airplanes, the controls would move in unison,
sentences.zh: 在其他商用飞机中，操纵杆会协同移动，

sentences.en: so that you would actually feel the moves your co-pilot was making on their controls.
sentences.zh: 这样你实际上能感觉到你的副驾驶在他们的操纵杆上做出的动作。

sentences.en: This design variation may also have contributed to what was about to become a very bad situation.
sentences.zh: 这种设计差异可能也是导致即将演变成非常糟糕局面的原因之一。

sentences.en: In any case, as the pilot in the right seat pulled back on his stick...
sentences.zh: 无论如何，当右座的飞行员向后拉动他的操纵杆时……

sentences.en: The airplane put its nose up and started to soar upward.
sentences.zh: 飞机抬起机头，开始向上冲去。

sentences.en: When stall protections are in place, the plane won't just warn you not to pitch it at such an extreme angle.
sentences.zh: 当失速保护生效时，飞机不仅会警告你不要以如此极端的角度俯仰。

sentences.en: It physically will not let you do it.
sentences.zh: 它在物理上根本不允许你这样做。

sentences.en: But remember, the plane had shifted into a mode in which it wasn't offering that underlying protection.
sentences.zh: 但请记住，飞机已经切换到了一种不提供底层保护的模式。

sentences.en: As the angle got steeper and steeper, the air couldn't flow smoothly across the wings, and the plane began to stall.
sentences.zh: 随着角度变得越来越陡，空气无法顺畅地流过机翼，飞机开始失速。

sentences.en: The plane was angled up, trying to gain altitude, but it actually began to lose altitude.
sentences.zh: 飞机机头朝上，试图获取高度，但实际上开始失去高度。

sentences.en: The plane couldn't prevent a stall, but it could still warn that a stall was happening.
sentences.zh: 飞机无法阻止失速，但它仍然可以发出失速正在发生的警告。

sentences.en: It would have sounded like this.
And you'd think that if you heard this alarm, someone would say,
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为，如果你听到这个警报，会有人说，

sentences.en: hey, I think we might be stalling.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我想我们可能要失速了。

sentences.en: At one point, one of the co-pilots did say,
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，其中一名副驾驶确实说过，

sentences.en: But he didn't say, we've stalled.
sentences.zh: 但他没有说，我们失速了。

sentences.en: And the man in the right seat who was flying the airplane, the junior co-pilot,
sentences.zh: 而坐在右座驾驶飞机的年轻副驾驶，

sentences.en: he would put the nose down a couple times and then bring it right back up again.
sentences.zh: 他把机头压下去几次，然后又立刻拉了上来。

sentences.en: The co-pilots began to ring frantically for the captain to come into the cockpit.
sentences.zh: 两位副驾驶开始疯狂按铃叫机长进驾驶舱。

sentences.en: At one point, one of them says,
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，其中一人说，

sentences.en: All kinds of alarms were going off.
sentences.zh: 各种各样的警报都在响。

sentences.en: One minute and 38 seconds after the episode started,
sentences.zh: 事件开始一分三十八秒后，

sentences.en: the captain came into the cockpit and asked,
The co-pilots did not say we were in a stall.
sentences.zh: 副驾驶没有说我们失速了。

sentences.en: Instead, one of them said, quote,
sentences.zh: 相反，其中一人说，原话是，

sentences.en: we've completely lost control of the airplane and we don't understand anything.
sentences.zh: 我们完全失去了对飞机的控制，我们什么都不懂。

sentences.en: The captain had walked into a difficult scene to understand.
sentences.zh: 机长走进了一个难以理解的现场。
他们在下降还是在爬升？

sentences.en: At times, they couldn't seem to figure it out.
sentences.zh: 有时他们似乎搞不清楚。

sentences.en: Finally, they seem to realize they're in a fast descent,
sentences.zh: 最后，他们似乎意识到自己正在急速下降，

sentences.en: losing thousands of feet per minute.
sentences.zh: 以每分钟数千英尺的速度失去高度。

sentences.en: The captain never assessed correctly what was going on.
sentences.zh: 机长从未正确评估正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: He wasn't there to drink coffee or suck his thumb.
sentences.zh: 他不是去喝咖啡或闲着没事干的。

sentences.en: But he was never able to figure out what was going on,
sentences.zh: 但他始终没能弄清楚到底发生了什么，

sentences.en: even though it should have been amply obvious what was going on.
sentences.zh: 尽管当时发生的事情本来应该显而易见。

sentences.en: it wasn't obvious to them what was going on.
sentences.zh: 他们对正在发生的事并没有察觉。

sentences.en: They didn't know they were in a stall.
sentences.zh: 他们并不知道飞机陷入了失速。
如果他们当时意识到了这一点，

sentences.en: the fix would have been clear.
sentences.zh: 解决办法本该一清二楚。
这是航校的入门必修课。

sentences.en: The recovery would have required them to put the nose down.
sentences.zh: 要恢复正常飞行，他们必须把机头压低。

sentences.en: And then pull out of the ensuing dive.
sentences.zh: 然后再从随后的俯冲中拉起飞机。

sentences.en: The plane continued falling down at a jaw-dropping pace,
sentences.zh: 飞机以令人瞠目结舌的速度继续下坠，

sentences.en: losing several thousands of feet per minute.
sentences.zh: 每分钟损失好几千英尺的高度。

sentences.en: But since they started at 37,000 feet,
sentences.zh: 但由于他们当时在 37000 英尺的高空，

sentences.en: for a while there was still time for a recovery.
sentences.zh: 所以在一段时间内，仍然有时间进行改出。

sentences.en: So for quite a long time,
sentences.zh: 因此，在相当长的一段时间里，

sentences.en: a normal crew would have been able to recover.
sentences.zh: 普通的机组人员本该能够化解危机。
在大约 16000 英尺的高空，

sentences.en: the best crew in the world only probably
sentences.zh: 世界上最优秀的机组人员大概也只有

sentences.en: would have been able to recover.
no crew would have been able to recover
sentences.zh: 任何机组人员都无力回天了，

sentences.en: because they simply didn't have the space beneath them
sentences.zh: 因为他们根本没有足够的下方空间

sentences.en: to execute the dive before hitting the water.
sentences.zh: 在坠海前完成俯冲改出。

sentences.en: But in any case, they never tried to do it.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，他们从未尝试过这么做。

sentences.en: And so they rode this airplane down,
sentences.zh: 就这样，他们任由飞机坠毁，

sentences.en: and finally expressing certainty that they were going to die.
sentences.zh: 最后甚至确信自己死定 了。

sentences.en: Four minutes and 20 seconds after the incident started.
sentences.zh: 在事故发生四分二十秒后。

sentences.en: They pancaked into the water at a very high descent rate.
sentences.zh: 他们以极高的下沉率重重地砸向水面。

sentences.en: And, of course, it killed everyone instantly.
sentences.zh: 当然，这瞬间夺去了所有人的生命。

sentences.en: Six years after the crash of Flight 447,
sentences.zh: 在 447 号航班坠毁六年之后，

sentences.en: what's clear is that the pilots didn't understand
sentences.zh: 显而易见的是，飞行员们并不明白
最大的问题在于，怎么会这样？

sentences.en: How could they have a computer yelling stall at them
